question:
Which type(s) of intermolecular force hold the molecules together in:
(a) methyl bromide, $\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$
(b) butane, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$
(c) hexanol, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{13}\text{OH}$ (5 marks)
Write the general formula and the molecular formula of each constituents of the typical alkane mixtures in petrol (contain C6 to C10 carbon atoms). (5 marks)

Indicate for each of the following unsaturated compounds whether they have cis-trans isomers or not:
(a) 1-bromo-1,2-dichloroethene
(b) but-1-ene
(c) 1,1-dichloropropene
(d) pent-2-ene
(e) buta-1,3-diene (5 marks)

Petroleum is separated into its fractions by fractional distillation and many of the fractions are then subjected to a process called cracking. Name the two types of cracking and state the conditions required for each. (5 marks)
An organic compound contains $29.3\%$ carbon, $5.7\%$ hydrogen and $65\%$ bromine. Calculate the empirical formula of the compound. $[\text{H}=1;\text{ C}=12;\text{ Br}=80]$ (5 marks)
What is enolization? (1 mark)
Give the structure of the keto-enol isomeric forms of ethanal and propanone. (4 marks)
Give the general molecular formula of dialkanoic acids. (1 mark)
Give the systematic name and structure of the first two members of the dialkanoic acid series. (4 marks)
Plastics that cannot be softened or melted by heat or pressure are known as?

Give the structure and IUPAC nomenclature of the monomer unit of each of the following polymers:
(i) $-(-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-)_n-$
(ii) $-(-\text{CH}_2-\text{CCl}_2-)_n-$ (5 marks)
Name the types of isomerism that can be exhibited by alkenes with four or more carbon atoms. (3 marks)
List two (2) general methods for the laboratory preparation of alkenes. (2 marks)
Name the type of isomerism found in disubstituted benzenes. (1 mark)
Draw and name the four (4) aromatic structural isomers of $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{10}$. (4 marks)

Identify the functional group(s) in the following compounds and the series to which they belong:
(i) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$
(ii) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$
(iii) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$
(iv) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$
(v) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$
(vi) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$
(vii) $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$
(viii) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OCH}_3$
(ix) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOR}$ (18 marks)

Classify the following reactions as addition, substitution, elimination or hydrolysis:
(i) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
(ii) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$
(iii) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3 + \text{H}_2 \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$
(iv) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(Br)CH}_3 + \text{OH}^- \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 + \text{Br}^-$ (8 marks)

Give the structures and names of the products of the addition of 2-methylbut-2-ene to:
(i) hydrogen
(ii) bromine
(iii) hydrogen chloride
(iv) aqueous potassium hydroxide (12 marks)

What class of alkanols are likely to be produced by the reduction of:
(i) Alkanoic acids
(ii) Alkanones
(iii) Alkanoates
(iv) Alkanal
(v) Alkanoic anhydride (10 marks)
Give the structure of the likely products of the reaction between methyl chloride and ammonia. (3 marks)
What are isomers?
Draw structural formulae of the alkene isomers with molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$ and name them. (11 marks)

For the reactions of hydrogen chloride with 2-methylpropene:
(i) draw the structure of the two (2) possible carbocation intermediates
(ii) explain which carbocation is the more stable
(iii) Give the formula and name of the major product
(iv) Give the formula and name of the minor product. (8 marks)

Which of these pair of IUPAC nomenclature is most likely to be correct?
(i) 2,3-dimethylpentane and 2-methyl-3-methylpentane
(ii) 3-methyl-3-ethylheptane and 3-ethyl-3-methylheptane
(iii) 2,3-dimethyl-4-ethylheptane and 4-ethyl-2,3-dimethylheptane (6 marks)
Draw the structures of the two straight-chain isomeric alkanols with molecular formula, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ (2 marks)

Draw the structures of the oxidation products obtained when the two isomeric alkanols are oxidised separately by acidified potassium heptaoxochromate(VI). Write equations for any reactions which occur, using $[\text{O}]$ to represent the oxidising agent. (6 marks)
Draw the structure and give the name of the alkanol with molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ which is resistant to oxidation by acidified potassium heptaoxochromate(VI). (2 marks)

State the possible products that could be formed when the following haloalkanes undergo elimination. If more than one product is formed, identify them and explain how each is formed.
(i) 1-bromobutane
(ii) 2-bromobutane
(iii) 1-bromo-2-methylpropane
(iv) 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (8 marks)

Ethanoic acid can be formed from bromoethane in two steps. Give reagents and conditions for each step. Include in your answer the name of the mechanism for the first step and an equation for the second step (8 marks)
